name: spec
description: Canonical behavioral-spec schema — engine-bundled, single source of truth. A spec is one requirement per file: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body, stored at .riglane/specs/<scope>/<domain>/<spec_id>.md. Describes the POST-MINT (stored-file) shape. Dual-use: spec_write validates committed specs against it (file-by-file); the engine composes the 'Spec format' section of step_begin authoring guidance FROM it. This is a struct-schema INSTANCE (format: markdown), NOT an ajv meta-schema. Do NOT copy per-workflow or per-project. Design: sub_tasks/spec-system-revision/design/spec-system.md §3.1 / §3.1a / §3.2.

required.description: Engine-minted identity <domain>-<NNN> (e.g. auth-001). Serial NNN is assigned by the engine after dedup — the agent never supplies it on create. Present in the stored file; validated on read/update/commit. (spec_write exempts this from the pre-mint pass.)
Cohesive subsystem grouping (e.g. auth, ui, rate-limit). lowercase, prefer one word, max ~2 hyphenated, ~20 chars, readable not cryptic. Becomes the spec_id prefix.
One-line human title of the requirement (the spec's name).
Mandatory one-sentence hint of WHAT the spec requires. The engine copies it verbatim into _index.json as the search/scan discriminator.
Authorial INTENT of scope (broad hint, NOT a closed file list): areas, components, behaviors, or path patterns the spec governs. Powers discovery (area-search) and dedup topology.

The single scope this spec belongs to (e.g. generic, or a declared scope). A spec lives in exactly one scope — its directory. SINGLE value, not a list (legacy multi-scope removed in v1). Engine validates scope == the directory it is stored in.

optional.description: Citations into the source document (e.g. '4.2 Rate Limits'). Strong dedup signal for extraction; absent for specs authored without a source document.

Cross-references to other specs. Bare id = same scope; qualified (web:auth-002) = cross-scope reference (a reference, not membership). May carry temp-keys during bulk authoring; the engine resolves them.
One-line description of the domain. Required ONLY when this spec introduces a NEW domain (enforced by spec_write, not here — a conditional the struct cannot express); ignored for an existing domain.
